title: Play a word on a Scrabble board from the rack: lay four tiles face up in their squares without jostling the others
instruction: Play the word PLANT down the board through the A that is already there: take the tiles P, L, N and T from the rack and lay each one face up, the right way round, in its square, without knocking the tiles already on the board out of place.
context: Nearly everyone has played Scrabble or watched it played at a family table. The catch every player knows: the tiles are small, smooth and loose on a flat board, so a careless hand shoves the words already played out of line and the game has to be put back together. To play a word the robot must take thin wooden tiles that stand leaning on the rack, each a finger's width from the next, turn each one from standing to lying face up with its letter the right way round, and set it down in a square whose neighbours are loose tiles 4 mm away. This is not a coin stood on edge into a slot and not block stacking: the parts are laid flat, in order, in a crowded grid, and the rest of the board and the rack are scored for staying put.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. One Hasbro Scrabble Classic Crossword Game (board, 100 wooden tiles, wooden racks). Published: tiles 19 x 19 x 4, board 15 x 15 squares. Estimates, to check with a ruler and a kitchen scale: squares at 23 pitch, board 380 square and 2 thick, a tile 1.0 g, the rack 190 long, 23 deep, 18 high and 31 g (190 x 18 x 23 is the listed size of retail wooden racks for these tiles), its groove leaning the tiles 30 degrees back. 1) Board: flat on the table, its near edge along x = 145, centred on y = 0, so the centre star is at (335, 0). Rows are counted from the robot (row 0 nearest, centre x = 174, each next row 23 further), columns from the robot's left (column 7 is the centre, y = 0; each next column 23 further right). Words read left to right and toward the robot for a player on the robot's side. 2) Already played, tiles face up and upright for that player, each centred in its square: THRONE down column 7 from the centre star (row 7) to row 2, and EXTRA along row 2 from column 7 to column 11, sharing the E. The A is at row 2, column 11: (220, -92). 3) Rack: on the table between the robot and the board, parallel to the board's edge, its front face along x = 105, centred on y = 0, tiles' faces toward the robot. Seven tiles stand on it, left to right P L N T O E I, at 27.5 spacing (8.5 gaps), the T at y = 0. 4) The play: P at row 4, L at row 3, N at row 1 and T at row 0 of column 11, that is (266, -92), (243, -92), (197, -92) and (174, -92). The squares beside them in columns 10 and 12 are empty. The four tiles of THRONE furthest from the robot lie beyond the arms' reach and are never needed. Frictions (estimates; tilt the board until a tile slides, about 19 degrees): wood on the printed board and wood on wood 0.35. Start: both arms at their ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Judged at the end of the run from a top photo and a ruler (in simulation from the poses). A played tile counts when it lies flat on the board face up, its centre is inside its own square (the square named in the setup), its letter is turned no more than 20 degrees from upright as the player on the robot's side reads it, no gripper is within 3 cm of it and it has not moved in the last second. Score 0 if none of P, L, N, T counts. Otherwise the score is the lowest of three numbers. Tiles: 1.0 if all four count, 0.7 if three, 0.4 if two, 0.2 if one. Board: measure how far each of the ten tiles that started on the board is from where it started (a tile turned over or no longer flat on the board is over 19 mm): 1.0 if none is over 5 mm; 0.5 if exactly one is over 5 mm and it is not over 19 mm; 0.2 otherwise. Rack: 1.0 if O, E and I all still stand on the rack, 0.6 otherwise. Doing nothing scores 0; tiles laid face down do not count; four tiles laid correctly while a starting tile was pushed a square away scores 0.2.
reset_notes: About 2 minutes. Keep a printed top photo of the start as the card. Lift the four played tiles off the board. Put any starting tile that moved back in the centre of its square, face up, upright for the player on the robot's side: THRONE down column 7 from the centre star, EXTRA along row 2 from its E. Set the rack back on its two tape marks (front face along x = 105 mm, centred between the arms) and stand the seven tiles in its groove, faces to the robot, in the order P L N T O E I from the robot's left, 27.5 mm apart with the T in the middle (a paper strip with seven ticks laid along the rack gives the spacing). Check from above that the board's near edge is still on its tape line. Return both arms to the ready pose. Nothing is used up; the set has spare tiles for any that get lost (a set costs about 20 to 25 US dollars, an estimate).
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Tiles are plain 19 x 19 x 4 mm blocks with sharp edges (real ones are slightly rounded) and uniform density; letters, point values and the board's squares are print only. The board is one flat, fixed sheet: its fold and any surface texture are not modelled. The rack is a loose wooden bar with a straight groove. Square pitch, board and rack sizes, the groove's shape and lean, masses and frictions are estimates.
